authoredFrom: Erlang semantics and OTP's own compiler, authored BEFORE the analyzer was run on this file. Erlang function identity is (name, arity) — ER-D2, and `erlc` itself: a file that declares `get/2` and writes `get(D)` is calling the AUTO-IMPORTED `erlang:get/1`, not its own function, and `setelement/3` is a BIF whether or not the file declares any `setelement`. `otp/lib/compiler/src/rec_env.erl` is the real instance: it declares `get/2` and calls `get(new_key_calls)` at lines 65-67, and the analyzer published `calls -> get` for all three. The positive rows are read off Erlang's resolution rule; the forbidden rows are the two auto-imports, which no compiler can bind to a local function.

expectRelationships.note: `get(key, D)` — arity 2 IS declared here, so this is the file's own function. This is the ONLY `calls -> get` edge the file may carry.
`emit(G, T, Def, V)` — arity 4 is the declared one.

forbidRelationships.note: ER-D45: `get(D)` is arity 1. The file declares `get/2`, so this is the auto-imported process-dictionary BIF `erlang:get/1` and it names no local function. A name-only gate published this edge in 618 places over the corpus (100 of them `get/1`); the shared oracle gates on name/arity, which is why these rows sat in `unexplained` with no explanation.
a BIF whose name is not declared here at all — the case the original bare-name gate already handled, pinned so the arity-exact gate keeps handling it

`emit("x")` is arity 1; the file declares `emit/4`. Nothing local binds it. The same shape as `get/1`, and the class OTP actually contains: `otp/lib/asn1/src/asn1ct_gen_check.erl` declares `emit/4` and calls `emit(" case ")`.
